text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.83% today, extending a sharp two-week rally of nearly 18% that's driven by rising oil prices and geopolitical tension in energy markets. Brent crude topped $106 a barrel after a deadly Saudi airport attack, and broader Middle East instability—including potential U.S. military involvement against Iran-backed Houthis—has kept crude prices elevated. Refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, near full utilization, which means the company benefits from both higher crude input costs and the ability to sell refined products (gasoline and diesel) at stronger margins when oil prices spike.

The rally also reflects tightening global energy supplies driven by geopolitical disruption; even the Trump administration's push to ease sanctions on Russian diesel to address domestic supply concerns has done little to dampen crude prices, suggesting the market sees lasting supply risk. With oil prices still up sharply over two weeks and refineries operating near capacity, refiners like Marathon are positioned to capture margin gains from processing expensive crude into sellable products.
